newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. bankers seek to buy Israel's Mercantile Bank.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bankers seek to buy Israel's Mercantile Bank.

text.p: Indiana bankers Hart and Mark Hasten are seeking to acquire Israel's Mercantile Discount Bank jointly with British investor Bernard Schreier, their representative in Israel said.
The Hastens met Finance Minister Dan Meridor two weeks ago to discuss the offer, said Shlomo Nass, an attorney who represents the Hastens in Israel.

Mercantile, one of Israel's smaller commercial banks, is controlled by Israel Discount Bank, Israel's third-largest bank. Discount has been under order by the government since 1993 to sell Mercantile to enhance competitiveness in the banking sector.

The sale, however, is on hold pending a suit by Schreier, who sought to acquire 50 percent of Mercantile from Britain's Barclay's Bank four years ago. He contends that Discount incorrectly used its right of first refusal to buy the Barclay's shares and is seeking a court ruling requiring Discount to sell the 50 percent to him.

The Hasten family is seeking to buy Mercantile together with Schreier, said Nass. They hope to reach an agreement under which Schreier agrees to drop the suit in exchange for Discount and the Israeli government's agreeing to sell him and the Hastens 100 percent of the bank.

The government, which controls Discount, will decide the terms of the Mercantile sale. Treasury officials were unavailable for comment, but Nass said: "I understand they have a positive view on it, but they have yet to make a decision."

This is the Hastens' second attempt at acquiring an Israeli bank. Earlier this year, they participated in a tender for Baron Edmund de Rothschild's controlling stake in Israel General Bank but were outbid by a South African group.
